newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU summit breaks for lunch, no stability deal yet.
newsitem.headline: EU summit breaks for lunch, no stability deal yet.

text.p: European Union leaders broke for lunch on the first day of their summit on Friday without an agreement on a pact to enforce budget discipline on countries that join a single European currency in 1999, diplomats said.

Finance ministers met separately to try to break a deadlock over German demands for tighter rules on the circumstances in which countries should be exempted from fines for running excessive budget deficits. The leaders were due to return to the issue after lunch, an EU diplomat said.
"It is a pretty tough fight, and that's an understatement," Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky told reporters after the morning session.

Diplomats said Bonn was demanding that budget sinners be subjected to automatic fines for running a deficit of more than three percent of gross domestic product unless their economy contracted by at least one percent in a year.
France and Spain argued that the EU's council of ministers must make a political judgment before any fines and sought a lower threshold for exceptions if GDP shrank by 0.75 percent.
EU diplomats said Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, who was chairing the two-day summit, was optimistic a deal could be wrapped up on the so-called stability pact.
